title: Smooth prime-to-characteristic curve calculation
statement:
Let $k$ be algebraically closed, let $C$ be a smooth separated finite-type
scheme of dimension at most one, and let
$\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$. All eight applicable assertions
$\mathcal C_r(C,\underline{\mathbf F_\ell})$ hold, and every field-extension
map and open-restriction map is the one induced by pullback of etale
cocycles.

proof.text: The constant Λ/rΛ sheaf is killed by r. On a connected smooth curve construct all eight fields from C1-C8. For C3 at a distinct prime use prime-annihilated primary cases and zero-object preservation by the explicitly additive coefficient-forgetting functor. For C4 and C6, split on (r:k) ≠ 0. In the equal-characteristic case invertible-order torsion forces source and inverse-image cohomology to be zero by the prime nonunit cohomology lemma. C5 and C7 use the existing proper calculations.

Finite-type curves are Noetherian. Index their clopen connected components by ConnectedComponents C, using a representative supplied by the proved surjectivity of the quotient map. Connected-component equality proves pairwise disjointness and coverage. Each component is a connected smooth IsCurve scheme: its Krull dimension is bounded by that of C, and the other morphism properties compose with the open inclusion. Apply the connected eight-field assembly to each component. This includes zero-dimensional components; the empty curve has an empty index.

Apply finite clopen constant-coefficient assembly to those component assertions, with the actual module Λ/rΛ. This returns the unchanged bundled statement, with the canonical cohomology maps and no signature modification.
